hops.title: Ask it: is a big puffy cloud alive?
hops.text: From a window, or outside with you close by, find a big puffy cloud. A puffy cloud can hold water that weighs about as much as 100 elephants! Ask, "It moves and gets bigger, so is it alive?" Expect a happy "yes." Then check your list together: does a cloud eat? Does it make baby clouds?

sources.citation: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, "How much does a cloud actually weigh?" (How Things Fly, 2014)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A parent and child seen from behind on a park path pointing up at a large white cumulus cloud in a blue sky.
image.caption: A puffy cloud can drift, grow and hold water as heavy as 100 elephants, yet it is not alive.

hops.title: Point at it: green moss on a shady rock
hops.text: On your walk, stay close and look, without picking, for fuzzy green moss on a shady rock. Here a living plant sits right on a rock that was never alive. Moss has no true roots. It soaks up water straight through its surface, and many kinds can rest when they dry out and grow again once they get wet.

sources.citation: National Park Service, Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, "Mosses and Liverworts" (2024)
Lloyd R. Stark et al., "Generational Differences in Response to Desiccation Stress in the Desert Moss Tortula inermis," Annals of Botany (2007)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A bright green cushion of moss speckled with raindrops growing on top of a shady gray stone beside a path.
image.caption: Living moss grows on a never-alive rock and soaks up rain straight through its surface.

hops.title: Say it: most plants move in slow motion
hops.text: Try: "Plants do move. Most just move in slow motion! A young sunflower turns from east to west all day to follow the sun, then swings back east at night." Use this line when your child says a quiet houseplant can't be alive because it never walks around the room.

sources.citation: Andy Fell, "Sunflowers Move by the Clock," University of California, Davis News (August 4, 2016)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A young sunflower in a sunlit garden leaning toward the rising morning sun.
image.caption: Young sunflowers slowly turn to follow the sun all day and swing back overnight.
